children.name: Magnipelta
children.description: Magnipelta — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Magnipelta mycophaga Pilsbry, 1953
children.description:
External: Light tan body and mantle with black spots; broad mantle covering most of dorsum with a black longitudinal stripe on either side; pneumostome posterior to middle of mantle (Forsyth 2004); keel present; no caudal mucus pore; sole is sometimes 3-part, sometimes not (Leonard et al. 2011).

Internal: Epiphallus present; buccal and tentacular retractors joined behind diaphragm (Leonard et al. 2011).

children.name: Prophysaon
children.description: Prophysaon — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Prophysaon andersonii
children.description: Prophysaon andersonii, common name the reticulate taildropper, is a species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusk in the family Ariolimacidae endemic to Western North America.

children.name: Prophysaon coeruleum Cockerell, 1890
children.description: Prophysaon coeruleum, (the blue-grey taildropper), is a species of slug belonging to the genus Prophysaon, a genus known for the autotomy of its tail.

children.name: Prophysaon dubium Cockerell, 1890
children.description:
External: Dorsal base color includes various shades of brown, reddish-brown, olive, and gray; mantle always mottled to some extent by areas of brown or gray pigment, which on some specimens merges to form broad, dark stripes; mantle and tail covered with numerous cone-shaped papillae; foot and to lesser extent the mantle, marked by light brown, orange, copper, and/or gold flecking; sole gray or cream.

Eggs: Translucent eggs are deposited in small clusters (6 to 14 eggs); approximately 1.3 x 1.2 mm diameter shortly after being laid and 2.1 x 1.5 mm 10 weeks later.

.

children.name: Prophysaon foliolatum
children.description: Prophysaon foliolatum, or the yellow-bordered taildropper, is a slug in the genus Prophysaon, native to North America, ranging from Alaska to Oregon.

children.name: Prophysaon obscurum Cockerell, 1890
children.description:
External: Body gray, very dark above, with or without obscure dark lateral bands on tail; mantle black; sole dark gray. typically olive colored.

Possibly a dark color variant of Prophysaon vanattae.

.

children.name: Prophysaon vanattae Pilsbry, 1948
children.description:
External: Color variable: whitish-buff, bluish-gray, or red on the back and gray-buff at the sides; body with a conspicuous black band on each side of the body laterally behind mantle, enclosing a lighter wedge-shaped dorsal area, which encloses a wedge shaped darker median stripe (sometimes faint); mantle colored buff or red with two curved lateral black bands (sometimes obsolete) above breathing hole, and scattered black markings; most specimens do not show the oblique constriction on the tail; head may extend to some distance past mantle; mantle is long; sole usually cream colored. Pilsbry (1948:699, fig. 380e) described a specimen of this species that has black mottling on the entire body and lacks the lateral side bands.

Internal: Epiphallus tapers; epiphallus contains two longitudinal ridges (Pilsbry 1948).

.

children.description: Anadenulus — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Hesperarion
children.description: Hesperarion — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Hesperarion mariae Branson, 1991
children.description:
External: Light red-gray body and mantle; lighter sides; darker head and neck; large, irregular black spots and marks on mantle; little black spots that may form lines along skin grooves; mantle forms a hump over internal shell; light and dark stripes on foot fringe; large, downward-bent caudal mucus pit; slightly 3-part, white sole (Branson 1991; Roth 2004).

Internal: Asymmetric internal shell; cylindrical penis with a large conical verge in the apex; large, thin-walled dart sac with one long, curved dart in the atrium; oviduct significantly longer than penis (Branson 1991; Roth 2004).

children.name: Hesperarion niger
children.description:
External: Black brown to red gray body and mantle, lighter on sides; small black spots on body, forming lines along mucus grooves; tan to gray foot fringe with black stripes; white to pale tan sole, sometimes with black spots on side portions; caudal mucus pore present (Roth 2004).

Internal: Internal shell asymmetric; cylindrical penis with narrow base, and retractor and epiphallus at apex; small conical verge in apex of penis; epiphallus of constant width; three large pilasters in atrium; appendix on base or dart sac of atrium; dart sac of atrium contains multiple curved darts (Roth 2004).

children.name: Hesperarion plumbeus B.Roth, 2004
children.description:
External: Mantle ~30% of body length; unicolor gray body, with lighter sides and neck and slight dark mottling on mantle; skin grooves slightly darkened; keel present; foot fringe light tan to gray, without strong stripes; light tan sole; caudal mucus pore present (Roth 2004).

Internal: Short penis, broader toward apex, and with internal teardrop-shaped verge; penial retractor on first bend of epiphallus; appendix next to free oviduct on atrium; long spermatheca duct, broader for first half of length than the second half; small, acorn-shaped spermatheca (Roth 2004).

Differs from H. niger, because penis is shorter and has a teardrop-shaped rather than conical verge (Roth 2004). .

children.name: Ariolimax
children.description: Ariolimax — a genus of gastropodas.

children.name: Ariolimax buttoni
children.description: Ariolimax buttoni is a species of banana slug native to the West Coast of the United States.

children.name: Ariolimax californicus J.G.Cooper, 1872
children.description: Ariolimax californicus, the California banana slug, is a species of terrestrial slug from the coast range of the San Francisco Peninsula.

children.name: Ariolimax columbianus
children.description: Ariolimax columbianus, the Pacific banana slug, is a species of slug found on the Pacific coast of North America.

children.name: Ariolimax dolichophallus Mead, 1943
children.description:
External: Slender, medium-sized Ariolimax; bright yellow, without spots (Harper 1988); slightly darker longitudinal grooves in skin; 3-part sole, wider than dorsum, and with side sections similar in color or slightly darker than middle section (Mead 1943).

Internal: Penis tubular, 60-110 mm long fully extended, with a flagellum-like apical section 2-4x the length of the basal thick portion; vas deferens follows along penis flagellum and joins apex; penis retractor attached at 1/4 to 1/3 from its base; short, curved vagina with a thin-walled and a thick-walled portion; spermatheca attached to vagina above the retentor muscles; short oviduct; short atrium (Mead 1943).
